name: Burton Memorial Tower
clues: You can hear this place before you see it.
It is one of the tallest things on Central Campus.
It has a clock face on each side.
A carillon is played from near the top.
It stands beside Hill Auditorium, at the edge of Ingalls Mall.

name: Michigan Stadium
clues: Most of this place sits below street level.
It is far busier on fall Saturdays than any other day.
It is on the athletic campus, south of Central Campus.
More than 100,000 people fit inside.
Its nickname is "The Big House."

name: Hatcher Graduate Library
clues: People come here to be quiet.
It faces the Diag.
It has a north and a south building.
It is connected to the Shapiro Undergraduate Library.
Students call it "the Grad."

name: The Cube
clues: This is a sculpture, not a building.
It balances on one corner.
Give it a push and it spins.
It sits in Regents' Plaza.
It is next to the Michigan Union.

name: Michigan Union
clues: Students have gathered here for more than a century.
It stands on State Street, at the end of South University Avenue.
It reopened in 2020 after a long renovation.
John F. Kennedy proposed the idea of the Peace Corps from its front steps in 1960.
It is the student union on Central Campus.

name: Michigan League
clues: It was built because women were once kept out of another campus building.
It opened in 1929.
It has a garden, a ballroom and an inn.
The Lydia Mendelssohn Theatre is inside.
It stands across Ingalls Mall from Burton Tower, on North University Avenue.

name: Hill Auditorium
clues: People come here to listen.
It is famous for its acoustics.
Albert Kahn designed it, and it opened in 1913.
It seats about 3,500 and has a huge pipe organ.
It is the big concert hall on North University Avenue, next to Burton Tower.

name: Rackham Building
clues: It is named for a Detroit lawyer who was an early investor in Ford Motor Company.
It closes off the north end of Ingalls Mall.
It has an auditorium, an amphitheatre and grand study halls.
Doctoral students defend their dissertations here.
It is the home of the graduate school.

name: Angell Hall
clues: Its front is a long row of tall stone columns.
It faces State Street.
It is named for the university's longest-serving president.
There is an observatory and planetarium on its roof.
The computing site called the Fishbowl is here.

name: Shapiro Undergraduate Library
clues: It stays open late into the night.
It is linked by a walkway to an older, bigger neighbor.
Bert's Cafe is on the first floor.
Its nickname is not a compliment.
Students call it the UGLi.

name: West Hall
clues: People walk through this building as well as into it.
It sits at the southeast corner of the Diag.
It was built for the engineering college.
Tradition says a kiss under its arch at midnight means you'll marry.
Its name is a compass direction, and its arch is called the Engineering Arch.

name: Museum of Art
clues: It is free to walk in.
It stands across State Street from the Michigan Union.
Its older half was built as Alumni Memorial Hall.
A glassy modern wing was added in 2009.
It goes by four letters: UMMA.

name: Law Quad
clues: It looks like it was borrowed from Oxford or Cambridge.
Its stone buildings went up in the 1920s and 1930s.
A gift from alumnus William W. Cook paid for it.
Its Reading Room has stained glass and a vaulted ceiling.
Future lawyers study here.

name: Ross School of Business
clues: A very large gift gave this school its current name in 2004.
It sits on the south side of Central Campus, along Tappan Avenue.
Its main building has a glass-roofed Winter Garden.
MBA and BBA students take classes here.
It is the business school.

name: The Diag
clues: Thousands of students cross it every day.
It is not a building.
Its name comes from the sidewalks that cut across it.
A brass block M is set into the pavement at its center.
It is the open space at the heart of Central Campus.

name: Biological Sciences Building
clues: Mastodons live here, sort of.
It is one of the newer buildings on Central Campus, opened in 2018.
It has a planetarium and dome theater.
The Museum of Natural History moved here from the Ruthven Building.
Its initials are BSB.

name: Nichols Arboretum
clues: No classes meet here, but students come anyway.
It slopes down to the Huron River.
It has a famous peony garden.
It sits just east of the Hill residence halls.
Everyone calls it the Arb.

name: The Rock
clues: It never looks the same for long.
It sits at the corner of Hill Street and Washtenaw Avenue.
Student groups come at night to cover it.
It is buried under countless layers of paint.
It is a boulder.

name: Crisler Center
clues: It is loudest in the winter.
It is next door to Michigan Stadium.
It opened in 1967.
It is named for a football coach, but football is not played here.
The basketball teams play here.

name: Yost Ice Arena
clues: It was built in the 1920s as a field house.
It is on South State Street.
It was converted for a different sport in 1973.
It is named for a legendary football coach.
The hockey team plays here.

name: Duderstadt Center
clues: It almost never closes.
It is on North Campus.
It was originally called the Media Union.
It holds a library, design labs and recording studios.
Students call it the Dude.

name: Lurie Bell Tower
clues: You can hear it across North Campus.
It was finished in 1996.
It holds a 60-bell carillon.
It stands near the Duderstadt Center.
It is North Campus's bell tower.

name: Pierpont Commons
clues: North Campus comes here to eat and hang out.
Blue buses stop right outside.
It used to be called the North Campus Commons.
It is named for a longtime university vice president.
It is the student union of North Campus.

name: South Quad
clues: More than a thousand students live here.
It opened in 1951.
Its dining hall is one of the largest on campus.
It is on East Madison Street, a short walk from the Michigan Union.
Its name is a compass direction — the opposite of north — plus "Quad."

name: East Quad
clues: Students live and take classes in the same building here.
It is the home of the Residential College.
It is on East University Avenue.
It reopened in 2013 after a full renovation.
Its name is the direction the sun rises, plus "Quad."

name: Mosher-Jordan Hall
clues: It is on the Hill.
It opened in 1930 as a women's residence hall.
It is named for two deans of women.
The Hill Dining Center is attached to it.
Its nickname is MoJo.

name: Bursley Hall
clues: It is the largest residence hall on its campus.
It is on North Campus.
It opened in 1967.
It has its own dining hall and sits next to the Baits houses.
It is named for a longtime dean of students, Joseph Bursley.

name: Power Center
aliases: Power Center for the Performing Arts
clues: Its glass front reflects the trees across the street.
It opened in 1971.
It is at Fletcher Street and Huron Street.
Plays, dance and musical theatre are staged here.
It is the Power Center for the Performing Arts.

name: Kelsey Museum of Archaeology
clues: What it holds is thousands of years older than the building.
It is on State Street, across from Angell Hall.
The stone building with a turret was once called Newberry Hall.
Inside are artifacts from ancient Egypt, Greece and Rome.
It is the archaeology museum.

name: Clements Library
clues: Its specialty is early American history.
It is on South University Avenue, next to the President's House.
Albert Kahn designed it, and it opened in 1923.
It holds rare books, maps and manuscripts.
It is named for regent William L. Clements.
